newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says not positively considering French deal.
newsitem.headline: NTT says not positively considering French deal.

text.p: Japanese telecoms giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) said on Thursday that it was not positively considering a possible investment in the French telecoms market.

"We're not in a situation to positively consider any such action. Everything is up in the air," a company official told Reuters when asked about a report in Britain's Financial Times that NTT is considering investing $500 million to buy 10 percent of French carrier Cegetel.
He would not elaborate on what he meant by "positively consider" and made no further comment.
Cegetel is a unit of Cie Generale des Eaux, and seen as the main rival to France Telecom.
British Telecommunications (BT) has a 25 percent stake in Cegetel. SBC Communications Inc of the United States and Germany's Mannesmann AG hold 15 and 10 percent stakes in the firm, respectively.

The paper said it was not clear whether NTT would take its stake out of BT's 25 percent share or replace one of the smaller shareholders. By enveloping NTT in joint investments, BT would hope to draw NTT into Concert, the alliance between BT and MCI, the U.S. long-distance carrier, the FT said.
